summary: Frontend-focused retest of 3 new Dashboard features per fresh-fork review request: (1) selection-persistence/stale-pinning fix, (2) new QuickTradePanel, (3) local bars caching/incremental fetch - plus regression pass. All 3 targeted features PASSED. Verified via live browser automation against the deployed preview URL with real login + Demo Mode: selecting a scanner row (LCID/PLUG/NIO/SOFI across runs) sets selected-symbol-header + highlights the row; waited a full 60s spanning both the 30s account poll and a 60s auto-scan cycle - the previously-selected symbol (PLUG) dropped out of live scan results but correctly stayed visible in the table with opacity-50 + a 'stale' badge (data-testid=stale-badge-PLUG) and the header/chart never lost the selection. QuickTradePanel renders next to the header with a qty input pre-filled to a calculated qty (e.g. 27 shares from $100/$3.7ish), an est-cost label, and a BUY button; clicking BUY fires POST /api/orders and the UI responds cleanly with a 'Buy X failed: Market is closed...' error toast (expected - real system clock is outside 4am-8pm ET) without hanging/crashing. No open position existed for the tested symbols so the SELL button correctly did not render (conditional logic verified in code, not exercised live). Bars caching confirmed via network interception: switching A->B->A repainted A's 1Day tile instantly (price label populated within 200ms, before any fresh network response could return) using the in-memory barsCache, and the subsequent background refetch + all periodic 30s refreshes correctly included a since=<ISO-timestamp> query param instead of re-fetching the full 100-bar window. Regression: login works, Dashboard/Scan/Trading(/trading route)/History/Settings all load with zero console errors; Trading page correctly shows the same 'Market is CLOSED' banner consistent with the Dashboard QuickTrade error. Previously-reported iteration_18 CRITICAL bug (missing merge_with_stream method causing 1Min/5Min tiles to show raw exception text) is confirmed FIXED - both tiles rendered real candlesticks with SMA20/SMA50/VWAP overlays in all test runs.

minor.issue: When a BUY order correctly triggers the intentional 400 'Market is closed' HTTPException (server.py line ~368), the outer broad `except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))` at the end of the same function (line ~646) catches this HTTPException too (since it IS an Exception) and re-wraps it as a 500 with detail becoming the string '400: Market is closed...'. So the client actually receives HTTP 500 instead of 400, even though the message text is correct. Confirmed via live browser network interception (response.status == 500, body.detail == '400: Market is closed. Extended trading hours...'). This is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this session's scope (not introduced by the reviewed changes), but contradicts the problem statement's claim that this was 'curl-verified... correctly rejects with 400'. Functionally harmless for the UI (axios/toast handles any non-2xx the same way and displays the error text fine), but violates proper REST status-code semantics and would break any client-side logic that specifically branches on status===400. Fix: re-raise HTTPException without modification in that except block, e.g. `except HTTPException: raise` before the generic `except Exception`.

action_items: (Optional, low priority, pre-existing/out-of-scope) In server.py's POST /api/orders handler, add `except HTTPException: raise` before the final `except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(500, ...)` so intentional 400/403 errors (market closed, risk-limit halts) aren't re-wrapped as 500. No UI impact currently since the frontend treats all non-2xx responses identically.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.js pinnedRow/displayResults logic (lines 19-38) is clean and correct - useEffect only updates pinnedRow when the symbol is still live in results, otherwise keeps the stale snapshot; displayResults synthesizes a `_stale: true` row only when needed. No edge-case bugs found.
QuickTradePanel.js correctly reuses the same localStorage risk-setting keys as Trading.js (verified by reading both files) so orders behave identically regardless of entry point, as intended.

MiniChartTile.js + barsCache.js: incremental refetch logic is well-reasoned (merge-by-timestamp, sorted ascending, capped at limit) and correctly falls back to a full fetch (no `since`) on first load. One micro-nit: `barsCache` is an in-memory Map with no size cap/TTL/eviction - fine for a single session but will grow unbounded if a user selects many different symbols/timeframes over a long trading day; not a functional bug today, just a minor long-session memory-growth note.

QuickTradePanel currentPrice fallback chain (trades[symbol]?.price || scanner row's current_price) is reasonable given MARKET_STREAM_ENABLED=false in this env means trades[symbol] will rarely populate - correctly falls back to the scanner-derived price so the panel still functions.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 new features for this session (selection persistence/stale pinning, QuickTradePanel, bars caching w/ since= incremental fetch) verified working correctly via live browser testing against the deployed preview URL, using Demo Mode + dashboard-scan-toggle to reliably get scanner candidates (note: demo scanner results are randomized/simulated and sometimes return 0-2 candidates per call depending on the criteria filter and RNG - this is expected simulated behavior, not a bug; if candidates are 0, retry the scan-toggle click or clear localStorage 'scannerCache'/'autoScan' first). Trading page route is '/trading' not '/trade' (nav link text 'Trade' routes there) - use nav click rather than direct URL nav to avoid false-negative blank-page results. Only remaining finding is a low-priority, out-of-scope, pre-existing backend status-code bug (400 Market-closed errors surfacing as 500) that does not affect UI behavior. No blocking issues found; safe to consider this session's 3 features + regression complete.
rca_of_the_issue: See backend_issues.minor above for the 500-vs-400 status code RCA. No RCA needed for frontend - no bugs found in the 3 new features under test.
